title: .*Does {product} support modeling in {sysmlv1}?*

meaning: documentation_heading; may describe absence or future work
title: No, {product} does not support modeling in SysML v1. It is designed specifically for SysML v2, making use of its updated metamodel, semantics, and services.

meaning: documentation_heading; may describe absence or future work
title: .*How do I integrate {product} with other tools or systems?*

meaning: documentation_heading; may describe absence or future work
title: {product} is a specialized tool for {sysmlv2}, focusing on the latest standards and methodologies, offering robust compatibility with {sysmlv2} through features such as textual notation support for model import or export, full compliance with the {sysmlv2} API for seamless integration with other tools, and ongoing integration efforts with Capella for enhanced model interoperability.

meaning: documentation_heading; may describe absence or future work

meaning: documentation_heading; may describe absence or future work
title: .*Does {product} support integration of a {sysmlv2} model with other models?*

meaning: documentation_heading; may describe absence or future work
title: {product} is designed to be extensible and can support the integration of {sysmlv2} models with other models or modeling tools, depending on the context.

meaning: documentation_heading; may describe absence or future work
title: .*Does {product} provide a capability to link data, trace data, across engineering domain using the {sysmlv2} API and Services?*

meaning: documentation_heading; may describe absence or future work
title: Yes, {product} is built on top of the SysML v2 API and Services, which provide capabilities for accessing, linking, and tracing data across engineering domains.
